answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond from a scarce, externally costly resource before it can vote or claim rewards; the protocol caps influence by bonded value, not account count, and slashes bonds when agents double-vote or break commitments. Spawning a thousand identities therefore adds no weight unless the attacker locks up a thousand bonds, which raises capital cost and exposes it to loss. A jetty of timber may cast a mirror-like shadow, but copying identities cannot copy the collateral.
